title: Annotatio V §.IV §.6: mandate+medium syllogism fails — not every command/medium absolutely necessary to salvation
pass_a_gloss: Here indeed I would wish, while the most Famous Professor feigns that I have contradicted myself, that he himself might at least seem to have said something. For what and of what sort, I ask, is this Reasoning: That fundamental Article is every and only one which in Sacred Scripture itself is held absolutely necessary to salvation either in express words or by evident Consequence; But the Article on the Sacred Supper has necessity of mandate, because the Sacred Supper is enjoined; And likewise necessity of Means, because Christ’s Body was given for us; Therefore the Article on the Sacred Supper is fundamental. I will not touch here all the poorly combined targets; this alone I will ask for the present from the Author: Whether whatever is commanded by God in Scripture, and so is said to have necessity of mandate, is therefore said in Sacred Scripture — either in express words or by evident Consequence — to be absolutely necessary to salvation? Or, what comes to the same: whether every Command of GOD is absolutely necessary to salvation? If so, how then will those be saved who before they eat of the Sacramental bread, of which the command is: Eat, this is my Body, meet their day? Is every Medium of salvation absolutely necessary to salvation? How then will Infants, even baptized, obtain salvation, if in infant age, incapable of the hearing of the divine word — the ordinary Medium of Salvation — they depart this life?
pass_b_english: The Author’s syllogism — mandate + means ⇒ fundamental Supper article — does not hold. Not every divine command is absolutely necessary to salvation (else who dies before eating the sacramental bread?).
Not every salvation-medium is absolute either — baptized infants die without hearing the word, the ordinary medium.
source_text: Hic equidem vellem, dum Clarissim. Professor me fingit ipsi mihi contradixisse, ipsemet saltem aliquid dixisse videri posset. Quæ enim qualísque quæso Ratiocinatio hæc: Articulus fundamentalis is omnis & solus est, qui in ipsâ Scriptura S. vel expressis verbis, vel per evidentem Consequentiam, ad salutem absolutè necessarius perhibetur; Articulus autem de S. Cœna necessitatem habet mandati, quia injuncta S. Cœna est; Itemque necessitatem Medii, quia Corpus Christi pro nobis datum est, Ergo Articulus de S. Cœna est fundamentalis. Non omnes hîc tangam scopas parum combinatas; hoc solum quæsivero in præsens ex Autore: Num, quodcunque in Scriptura à Deo mandatum est, eóque necessitatem mandati dicitur habere, idcirco vel conceptis verbis, vel per evidentem Consequentiam, ad salutem absolutè necessarium in Script. S. dictum sit? Vel, quod eôdem redit: num omne Mandatum DEI, absolutè necessarium ad salutem sit? Quodsi hoc; quî ergo isti salvabuntur, qui antequam manducant de pane Sacramentali, de quo mandatum est: Edite hoc est Corpus meum, diem suum obeunt? Num omne Medium salutis, absolutè necessarium ad salutem est? Quomodo igitur Infantes, etiam baptizati, salutem consequentur, si in ætate infantili, auditûs verbi divini, ordinarii Salutis medii, incapaces, ex hac vita discedant?
